findings.title: OAuth token exchange omits redirect_uri, causing GitHub OAuth to fail.
findings.body: The token exchange request to GitHub's OAuth access token endpoint does not include the `redirect_uri` parameter, even though it was included in the authorization URL (line 407). GitHub requires that if `redirect_uri` was provided in the authorization request, the same value must be sent in the token exchange. Without it, GitHub returns an `error=redirect_uri_mismatch` and no access token, causing the installation pipeline to always fail. The token body will not contain `access_token`, leading to the generic error response. Must add `redirect_uri` to the data dict.

findings.title: User mismatch check crashes when integration metadata lacks sender info.
findings.body: The new check compares `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` but does not guard against missing `sender` key. Integrations created before this change, or created via the Sentry pipeline without receiving the GitHub installation webhook event, will not have `sender` in their metadata. This will raise a `KeyError`, causing a 500 Internal Server Error instead of a handled error response. The code should check for the presence of `sender` (and `sender.get("login")`) before accessing, and either skip validation or return a specific error.

findings.title: get_user_info API call can raise unhandled exceptions.
findings.body: After obtaining an access token, the code calls `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` without catching `ApiError` or other exceptions that may occur if the token is invalid, GitHub API is down, or network issues. This will propagate up and result in a 500 error instead of the intended friendly error page. Wrap the call in a try/except and return the error response on failure.
